newsitem.title: GERMANY: German networks spar over public funding.
newsitem.headline: German networks spar over public funding.

text.p: The heads of German public broadcasting network ARD and private stations' lobby (VPRT) on Wednesday battled publicly over whether two new public stations can receive viewer fees.

The European Commission will decide in mid-June if the German channels Phoenix and the Kinderkanal, run jointly by public networks ARD and ZDF, are also eligible to receive state-mandated fees that the two networks obtain.
VPRT President Juergen Doetz told the Sueddeutsche Zeitung in an interview that an EU decision to allow the fee-financing would amount to a "collective prostration before public broadcasters".
"These stations (Phoenix and the Kinderkanal) are the result of a failure to heed European fair competition and subsidy rules," Doetz said.
"We were not able to succeed in convincing those in the German debate that the financing of these channels with fees is inadmissible," Doetz added.
The VPRT has lodged a complaint with the EU Commission against the use of public funding to support Phoenix, which carries events and documentaries, and the Kinderkanal children's network.
ARD Chairman Udo Reiter blasted the VPRT in a statement, accusing it of trying to use EU regulations to squeeze its programming out of the German television market.

"If the VPRT expects public broadcasters to leave the market of opinions just to commercial interests, then it made its estimation without us or the viewers," Reiter said. "We will defend ourselves -- also in Brussels -- with all means available."
Reiter added that public-supported programming presents only a 28 percent share of the German TV market.
